newsitem.title: JAPAN: Indices don't indicate slowdown - EPA. [CORRECTED 07:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Indices don't indicate slowdown - EPA. [CORRECTED 07:52 GMT]

text.p: The weakness in Japan's diffusion indices for leading and coincident indicators in April (Corrects from May) does not point to a slowdown in the nation's economic recovery, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told a news conference on Friday.
"From a long-term perspective this is just a temporary dip in Japan's recovery," he said.

Nukaya said the EPA did not just base its assessment of the economy on the numbers that came out of the diffusion indices. He said it was necessary to look at other factors, in this case, the rise in the sales tax on April 1.

The EPA earlier announced that the April index of leading indicators stood at 5.6 on a scale on 100 in April while the coincident index fell below 50 for the first time in eight months to 10.0 on a scale of 100.
A figure below the so-called "boom-or-bust" mark of 50 in the leading index is generally taken to mean the economy will contract in the coming months.
